name: Electricity: NG Boiler For FRCC
Conversion Process NRP-Derived ULSD (Pyrolysis and Upgrading Both On-Site- Including Pretreatment) Non-Combustion Emissions
Benzene byproduct from cracker plants (High-value chemical allocation, Integration of feedstock and cracker portions)
notes:
This method was established by Plastics Europe (2012) to estimate the impacts of steam cracker products with high commercial value (hydrogen, ethylene, propylene, butadiene, benzene, toluene, styrene, xylene, and ethylbenzene).
The impacts of feedstocks (i.e., ethane, propane, butane, natural gas liquids, naphtha) are allocated by using the traditional mass allocation, where all the co-products are accounted in the estimation of the mass allocation factors. 
The impacts associated with cracker operations (combustion of fuels, water for vapor generation, and non-combustion emissions) are allocated using an adapted mass allocation method, that only considers co-products with high commercialization value to calculate the allocation factors. These high-value products include hydrogen, ethylene, propylene, butadiene, benzene, toluene, styrene, xylene, and ethylbenzene.
Plastics Europe (2012) Eco profiles and Environmental Product Declarations of the European Plastics Manufacturers. Ethylene, Propylene, Butadiene, Pyrolysis Gasoline, Ethylene Oxide (EO), Ethylene Glycols (MEG, DEG, TEG) 
https://legacy.plasticseurope.org/application/files/8315/1783/7824/20130114101708-plasticseurope_eco-profile_ethylene__others_2012-11.zip (Accessed August 8, 2023).
